items.title: methods from a blanket impl over a NESTED binder - `switch_some`, `and_then` (`impl type F: Flow<Option<type T>>`) - are not offered on a `MemoCell<Option<T>>` receiver, though the checker resolves them
items.body: Probe (v0.43.0): `fun pick(m: MemoCell<Option<i32>>) { m.switch_some(..); m.and_then(..); m.distinct(); }` CHECKS clean, so the solver admits the blankets for `MemoCell`. The editor's member list does not show them. The owner's hypothesis: the `impl type F: Flow<Option<type T>>` form - completion's applicability test for a blanket whose bound carries a nested `type T` binder (or a bound on the binder, `type T: PartialEq`) fails where the solver's succeeds. Establish first which receivers miss (MemoCell vs SignalCell vs a pipe node vs `dyn Source`), and whether hover and signature help on such a call miss too. The fix should ASK THE SOLVER (the same admission the checker runs) instead of keeping a second applicability rule in vilan-ide. Pins: completion on `MemoCell<Option<T>>`, `SignalCell<Option<T>>`, `MemoCell<bool>` (`then_some`), and a negative (`switch_some` not offered on `MemoCell<i32>`).

items.title: the import quick fix is not offered in some positions: a STRUCT INITIALIZER's head (`MemoCell { cell = .. }`) and a MATCH CASE's pattern (`TransientState::Ready(..) =>`, `Route::Login =>`)
items.body: An unresolved name in an expression or a type annotation gets 'import std::..::Name'; the same name as the head of a struct literal, or as the path head of a match pattern, gets no code action. Likely the diagnostics at those sites carry a different code (or no 'cannot find' data) than the one the import action keys on. Census every position an unresolved type/variant/function name can stand in - struct literal head, pattern head (match, `is`, `let`), `impl` subject and `with` trait, generic argument, bound, attribute name (`[derive(X)]`), static call receiver (`Name::new()`), element tag - and pin the import action at each. B520's quick fixes ride the same code-action path.

items.discussion: owner 2026-10-03; proposal/store.md (S1–S6 do not cover the wire); A152 (the client-side wait); A149; kolt `store.vl`/`model.vl` (id-keyed field rpcs answering `Option`)
items.title: a MIRRORED `Store`: the server holds a `Store<Record>`, the client mirrors it, frames are PER-FIELD patches - so a snapshot is sent once, a rename sends one string, and a field handle reached through its parent is not a maybe type
items.body:
The owner's rule: an rpc for a granular field that can be called where the parent does not exist must answer a maybe type; a field reached THROUGH the parent struct need not, since the struct must exist to be passed and the field source is disposed when the parent's derivation turns `None`. Amendment: holding the struct proves the parent existed when the client last heard - a delete can cross a field call on the wire - so the WIRE answer stays a maybe; the client model hides it (inside the parent's scope an `Absent` field means the scope is about to be disposed: hold the last value). The first value is the catch: a field mirror has nothing until its first frame, so a non-optional `Source` needs a WAIT (A152) or a SEED (the snapshot carries the field's current value; the handle starts from it and follows its own channel). Seeding costs transfer only while the snapshot is the unit of update. The paper: `Store` over `std::rpc` - what a `[rpc]` returning `Store`/`StoreSome

` puts on the wire (the seed frame, then slot-addressed patches), how leases map to slots (per-subscription slots are already the store's unit), keyed and sequence nodes (after A149 S3), identity and the contract hash, reconnect (re-seed), and what kolt's `GlobalStore` and `model.vl` become. Doors and recs; probes on v0.43.0.
